                      - text: Just came across a fascinating open source project called PentAGI.
                      - text: It is essentially a fully autonomous AI red team where multiple AI agents collaborate, plan attacks, and attempt to exploit a target system.                       - text: This is a glimpse of where cybersecurity and AI are heading.
                      - text: "Red teaming is slowly shifting from manual testing to systems where AI can:"
                      - text: • analyze targets
                      - text: • coordinate attack strategies
                      - text: • execute testing workflows
                      - text: • report vulnerabilities
                      - text: Projects like this raise two important questions.
                      - text: How will organizations defend against AI powered attackers?
                      - text: And how can security teams use the same technology to stay ahead?

                      - text: "I'm a Software Engineer with 7+ years of industry experience, now at AWS. I've onboarded to CloudWatch, EC2 and Region Services. It never gets easier. You just get better at it. If you're joining a new team or starting a new role, here's what to do in your first 90 days:"
                      - text: "► Month 1: Absorb"
                      - text: → Set up your dev environment and document every issue you hit
                      - text: → Read the design docs and wiki pages for your team's services
                      - text: → Trace one request end-to-end through the system
                      - text: → Shadow on-call and listen to how incidents are handled
                      - text: → Ask "why was it built this way?" not "why isn't this better?"
                      - text: → Use AI tools to ramp up faster, feed it your team's docs, codebase, and wikis
                      - text: "► Month 2: Contribute"
                      - text: → Pick up small bugs and operational improvements
                      - text: → Review PRs — even if you're learning as you review
                      - text: → Document what confused you — your fresh eyes are valuable
                      - text: → Deploy something small to understand the pipeline
                      - text: → Build relationships across the team, not just with your manager
                      - text: "► Month 3: Own"
                      - text: → Take on a project you can own end-to-end
                      - text: → Volunteer for on-call
                      - text: → Become the go-to person for one area
                      - text: → Help onboard the next new person
                      - text: → Respect what came before you — offer suggestions, not demands
                      - text: The biggest mistake engineers make when joining a new team?
                      - text: Trying to prove themselves too fast.
                      - text: Slow down. Learn the system. Earn trust. Then lead.

                      - text: "I'm a Software Engineer with 7+ years of industry experience, now at AWS. I've onboarded to CloudWatch, EC2 and Region Services. It never gets easier. You just get better at it. If you're joining a new team or starting a new role, here's what to do in your first 90 days:"
                      - text: "► Month 1: Absorb"
                      - text: → Set up your dev environment and document every issue you hit
                      - text: → Read the design docs and wiki pages for your team's services
                      - text: → Trace one request end-to-end through the system
                      - text: → Shadow on-call and listen to how incidents are handled
                      - text: → Ask "why was it built this way?" not "why isn't this better?"
                      - text: → Use AI tools to ramp up faster, feed it your team's docs, codebase, and wikis
                      - text: "► Month 2: Contribute"
                      - text: → Pick up small bugs and operational improvements
                      - text: → Review PRs — even if you're learning as you review
                      - text: → Document what confused you — your fresh eyes are valuable
                      - text: → Deploy something small to understand the pipeline
                      - text: → Build relationships across the team, not just with your manager
                      - text: "► Month 3: Own"
                      - text: → Take on a project you can own end-to-end
                      - text: → Volunteer for on-call
                      - text: → Become the go-to person for one area
                      - text: → Help onboard the next new person
                      - text: → Respect what came before you — offer suggestions, not demands
                      - text: The biggest mistake engineers make when joining a new team?
                      - text: Trying to prove themselves too fast.
                      - text: Slow down. Learn the system. Earn trust. Then lead.

                      - text: "I'm a Software Engineer with 7+ years of industry experience, now at AWS. I've onboarded to CloudWatch, EC2 and Region Services. It never gets easier.                       - text: "► Month 1: Absorb"
                      - text: → Set up your dev environment and document every issue you hit
                      - text: → Read the design docs and wiki pages for your team's services
                      - text: → Trace one request end-to-end through the system
                      - text: → Shadow on-call and listen to how incidents are handled
                      - text: → Ask "why was it built this way?" not "why isn't this better?"
                      - text: → Use AI tools to ramp up faster, feed it your team's docs, codebase, and wikis
                      - text: "► Month 2: Contribute"
                      - text: → Pick up small bugs and operational improvements
                      - text: → Review PRs — even if you're learning as you review
                      - text: → Document what confused you — your fresh eyes are valuable
                      - text: → Deploy something small to understand the pipeline
                      - text: → Build relationships across the team, not just with your manager
                      - text: "► Month 3: Own"
                      - text: → Take on a project you can own end-to-end
                      - text: → Volunteer for on-call
                      - text: → Become the go-to person for one area
                      - text: → Help onboard the next new person
                      - text: → Respect what came before you — offer suggestions, not demands
                      - text: The biggest mistake engineers make when joining a new team?
                      - text: Trying to prove themselves too fast.

                      - text: enters an IPO this year, it could become one of the most valuable companies on the planet. More importantly, it would signal to the world that space is not a niche industry — it's the invisible backbone of modern civilisation. That kind of event could draw enormous follow-on investment into the sector.
                      - text: 🛰️ Sovereign launch capability matters more than ever
                      - text: Europe is increasingly focused on independent launch capability that doesn't rely on the US. One strong candidate for Europe's gateway to space is
                      - link "SaxaVord Spaceport" [ref=e920] [cursor=pointer]:

                      - text: During the same panel,

                      - text: explained their hybrid propulsion system using paraffin (yes, literal candle wax) and liquid oxygen.
                      - text: Because paraffin is inert, the fuel is far safer to store and transport. Less liquid propellant also means fewer turbopumps, fewer moving parts, and overall cheaper launch systems. It may also offer environmental advantages compared to traditional propulsion.
                      - text: I had some great follow-up discussions about this with

                      - text: 👨‍🚀 Human spaceflight is worth all the effort
                      - text: In a fascinating conversation with NASA Chief Health and Medical Officer James "JD" Polk, we discussed the risks of human spaceflight.
                      - text: While it is expensive and dangerous, the perspectives gained from human exploration — and humanity's innate drive to explore — make it worth continuing to push forward.
                      - text: ☁️ Orbital data centers are fascinating… but not imminent
                      - text: A talk by
                      - link "Gareth Stokes" [ref=e938] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/in/garethstokes/
                        - strong [ref=e940]: Gareth Stokes
                      - text: explored the idea of orbital data centers. In theory they offer advantages like unlimited solar power, natural cooling, physical security, and vast space for infrastructure.
                      - text: However, the economics aren't there yet. Even optimistic estimates suggest launching the required ~30 million kg to orbit would cost over $80 billion.
                      - text: "The biggest thing I took away from this event:"

                      - text: I'm convinced 2026 will redefine the global space sector.
                      - text: I spent the last two days at

                      - text: London exchanging ideas and having fascinating conversations with industry leaders.
                      - text: "Here are my biggest takeaways:"
                      - text: 🚀
                      - link "SpaceX" [ref=e914] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/spacex/
                        - strong [ref=e916]: SpaceX
                      - text: going public would be massive
                      - text: If
                      - link "SpaceX" [ref=e917] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/spacex/
                        - strong [ref=e919]: SpaceX
                      - text: enters an IPO this year, it could become one of the most valuable companies on the planet. More importantly, it would signal to the world that space is not a niche industry — it's the invisible backbone of modern civilisation. That kind of event could draw enormous follow-on investment into the sector.
                      - text: 🛰️ Sovereign launch capability matters more than ever
                      - text: Europe is increasingly focused on independent launch capability that doesn't rely on the US. One strong candidate for Europe's gateway to space is
                      - link "SaxaVord Spaceport" [ref=e920] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/saxavord/

                      - link "Debbie Strang" [ref=e923] [cursor=pointer]:

                        - strong [ref=e925]: Debbie Strang
                      - text: .
                      - text: 🔥 Hybrid propulsion could be Europe's opportunity
                      - text: During the same panel,
                      - link "Alfie Marturano" [ref=e926] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/in/alfie-marturano-b6964916/
                        - strong [ref=e928]: Alfie Marturano
                      - text: of
                      - link "HyImpulse" [ref=e929] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/hyimpulse/
                        - strong [ref=e931]: HyImpulse
                      - text: explained their hybrid propulsion system using paraffin (yes, literal candle wax) and liquid oxygen.
                      - text: Because paraffin is inert, the fuel is far safer to store and transport. Less liquid propellant also means fewer turbopumps, fewer moving parts, and overall cheaper launch systems. It may also offer environmental advantages compared to traditional propulsion.
                      - text: I had some great follow-up discussions about this with
                      - link "Ylenia M." [ref=e932] [cursor=pointer]:

                      - text: 👨‍🚀 Human spaceflight is worth all the effort
                      - text: In a fascinating conversation with NASA Chief Health and Medical Officer James "JD" Polk, we discussed the risks of human spaceflight.
                      - text: While it is expensive and dangerous, the perspectives gained from human exploration — and humanity's innate drive to explore — make it worth continuing to push forward.
                      - text: ☁️ Orbital data centers are fascinating… but not imminent
                      - text: A talk by
                      - link "Gareth Stokes" [ref=e938] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/in/garethstokes/
                        - strong [ref=e940]: Gareth Stokes
                      - text: explored the idea of orbital data centers. In theory they offer advantages like unlimited solar power, natural cooling, physical security, and vast space for infrastructure.
                      - text: However, the economics aren't there yet. Even optimistic estimates suggest launching the required ~30 million kg to orbit would cost over $80 billion.
                      - text: "The biggest thing I took away from this event:"
                      - text: The space industry is entering an incredibly exciting phase.
                      - text: Ambitious people, bold engineering challenges, and entirely new industries are forming right now — and I can't wait to be part of it.

                      - text: I'm convinced 2026 will redefine the global space sector.
                      - text: I spent the last two days at
                      - link "Space-Comm" [ref=e911] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/space-comm-expo/
                        - strong [ref=e913]: Space-Comm
                      - text: London exchanging ideas and having fascinating conversations with industry leaders.
                      - text: "Here are my biggest takeaways:"
                      - text: 🚀
                      - link "SpaceX" [ref=e914] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/spacex/
                        - strong [ref=e916]: SpaceX
                      - text: going public would be massive
                      - text: If
                      - link "SpaceX" [ref=e917] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/spacex/
                        - strong [ref=e919]: SpaceX
                      - text: enters an IPO this year, it could become one of the most valuable companies on the planet. More importantly, it would signal to the world that space is not a niche industry — it's the invisible backbone of modern civilisation. That kind of event could draw enormous follow-on investment into the sector.
                      - text: 🛰️ Sovereign launch capability matters more than ever
                      - text: Europe is increasingly focused on independent launch capability that doesn't rely on the US. One strong candidate for Europe's gateway to space is
                      - link "SaxaVord Spaceport" [ref=e920] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/saxavord/
                        - strong [ref=e922]: SaxaVord Spaceport
                      - text: ", whose remote geography makes it uniquely suited for launches — a point highlighted in a brilliant panel with"
                      - link "Debbie Strang" [ref=e923] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/in/debbiestrang/
                        - strong [ref=e925]: Debbie Strang
                      - text: .
                      - text: 🔥 Hybrid propulsion could be Europe's opportunity
                      - text: During the same panel,
                      - link "Alfie Marturano" [ref=e926] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/in/alfie-marturano-b6964916/
                        - strong [ref=e928]: Alfie Marturano
                      - text: of
                      - link "HyImpulse" [ref=e929] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/hyimpulse/
                        - strong [ref=e931]: HyImpulse
                      - text: explained their hybrid propulsion system using paraffin (yes, literal candle wax) and liquid oxygen.
                      - text: Because paraffin is inert, the fuel is far safer to store and transport. Less liquid propellant also means fewer turbopumps, fewer moving parts, and overall cheaper launch systems. It may also offer environmental advantages compared to traditional propulsion.
                      - text: I had some great follow-up discussions about this with
                      - link "Ylenia M." [ref=e932] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/in/ylenia-mami/
                        - strong [ref=e934]: Ylenia M.
                      - text: and

                        - strong [ref=e937]: Titto Ephraim Mathew
                      - text: .
                      - text: 👨‍🚀 Human spaceflight is worth all the effort
                      - text: In a fascinating conversation with NASA Chief Health and Medical Officer James "JD" Polk, we discussed the risks of human spaceflight.
                      - text: While it is expensive and dangerous, the perspectives gained from human exploration — and humanity's innate drive to explore — make it worth continuing to push forward.
                      - text: ☁️ Orbital data centers are fascinating… but not imminent
                      - text: A talk by
                      - link "Gareth Stokes" [ref=e938] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/in/garethstokes/
                        - strong [ref=e940]: Gareth Stokes
                      - text: explored the idea of orbital data centers. In theory they offer advantages like unlimited solar power, natural cooling, physical security, and vast space for infrastructure.
                      - text: However, the economics aren't there yet. Even optimistic estimates suggest launching the required ~30 million kg to orbit would cost over $80 billion.
                      - text: "The biggest thing I took away from this event:"
                      - text: The space industry is entering an incredibly exciting phase.
                      - text: Ambitious people, bold engineering challenges, and entirely new industries are forming right now — and I can't wait to be part of it.

                      - text: London exchanging ideas and having fascinating conversations with industry leaders.
                      - text: "Here are my biggest takeaways:"
                      - text: 🚀
                      - link "SpaceX" [ref=e914] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/spacex/
                        - strong [ref=e916]: SpaceX
                      - text: going public would be massive
                      - text: If
                      - link "SpaceX" [ref=e917] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/spacex/
                        - strong [ref=e919]: SpaceX
                      - text: enters an IPO this year, it could become one of the most valuable companies on the planet. More importantly, it would signal to the world that space is not a niche industry — it's the invisible backbone of modern civilisation. That kind of event could draw enormous follow-on investment into the sector.
                      - text: 🛰️ Sovereign launch capability matters more than ever
                      - text: Europe is increasingly focused on independent launch capability that doesn't rely on the US. One strong candidate for Europe's gateway to space is
                      - link "SaxaVord Spaceport" [ref=e920] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/saxavord/
                        - strong [ref=e922]: SaxaVord Spaceport
                      - text: ", whose remote geography makes it uniquely suited for launches — a point highlighted in a brilliant panel with"
                      - link "Debbie Strang" [ref=e923] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/in/debbiestrang/
                        - strong [ref=e925]: Debbie Strang
                      - text: .
                      - text: 🔥 Hybrid propulsion could be Europe's opportunity
                      - text: During the same panel,
                      - link "Alfie Marturano" [ref=e926] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/in/alfie-marturano-b6964916/
                        - strong [ref=e928]: Alfie Marturano
                      - text: of
                      - link "HyImpulse" [ref=e929] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/hyimpulse/
                        - strong [ref=e931]: HyImpulse
                      - text: explained their hybrid propulsion system using paraffin (yes, literal candle wax) and liquid oxygen.
                      - text: Because paraffin is inert, the fuel is far safer to store and transport. Less liquid propellant also means fewer turbopumps, fewer moving parts, and overall cheaper launch systems. It may also offer environmental advantages compared to traditional propulsion.
                      - text: I had some great follow-up discussions about this with
                      - link "Ylenia M." [ref=e932] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/in/ylenia-mami/
                        - strong [ref=e934]: Ylenia M.
                      - text: and
                      - link "Titto Ephraim Mathew" [ref=e935] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/in/tittoephraimmathew/
                        - strong [ref=e937]: Titto Ephraim Mathew
                      - text: .
                      - text: 👨‍🚀 Human spaceflight is worth all the effort
                      - text: In a fascinating conversation with NASA Chief Health and Medical Officer James "JD" Polk, we discussed the risks of human spaceflight.
                      - text: While it is expensive and dangerous, the perspectives gained from human exploration — and humanity's innate drive to explore — make it worth continuing to push forward.
                      - text: ☁️ Orbital data centers are fascinating… but not imminent
                      - text: A talk by
                      - link "Gareth Stokes" [ref=e938] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/in/garethstokes/
                        - strong [ref=e940]: Gareth Stokes
                      - text: explored the idea of orbital data centers. In theory they offer advantages like unlimited solar power, natural cooling, physical security, and vast space for infrastructure.
                      - text: However, the economics aren't there yet. Even optimistic estimates suggest launching the required ~30 million kg to orbit would cost over $80 billion.
                      - text: "The biggest thing I took away from this event:"
                      - text: The space industry is entering an incredibly exciting phase.
                      - text: Ambitious people, bold engineering challenges, and entirely new industries are forming right now — and I can't wait to be part of it.

                      - text: 🛰️ Sovereign launch capability matters more than ever
                      - text: Europe is increasingly focused on independent launch capability that doesn't rely on the US. One strong candidate for Europe's gateway to space is

                      - text: explained their hybrid propulsion system using paraffin (yes, literal candle wax) and liquid oxygen.
                      - text: Because paraffin is inert, the fuel is far safer to store and transport. Less liquid propellant also means fewer turbopumps, fewer moving parts, and overall cheaper launch systems. It may also offer environmental advantages compared to traditional propulsion.

                      - text: In a fascinating conversation with NASA Chief Health and Medical Officer James "JD" Polk, we discussed the risks of human spaceflight.
                      - text: While it is expensive and dangerous, the perspectives gained from human exploration — and humanity's innate drive to explore — make it worth continuing to push forward.
                      - text: ☁️ Orbital data centers are fascinating… but not imminent
                      - text: A talk by
                      - link "Gareth Stokes" [ref=e938] [cursor=pointer]:

                      - text: explored the idea of orbital data centers. In theory they offer advantages like unlimited solar power, natural cooling, physical security, and vast space for infrastructure.
                      - text: However, the economics aren't there yet. Even optimistic estimates suggest launching the required ~30 million kg to orbit would cost over $80 billion.

                      - text: going public would be massive

                      - text: enters an IPO this year, it could become one of the most valuable companies on the planet. More importantly, it would signal to the world that space is not a niche industry — it's the invisible backbone of modern civilisation. That kind of event could draw enormous follow-on investment into the sector.
                      - text: 🛰️ Sovereign launch capability matters more than ever
                      - text: Europe is increasingly focused on independent launch capability that doesn't rely on the US. One strong candidate for Europe's gateway to space is

                      - text: During the same panel,

                      - text: explained their hybrid propulsion system using paraffin (yes, literal candle wax) and liquid oxygen.
                      - text: Because paraffin is inert, the fuel is far safer to store and transport. Less liquid propellant also means fewer turbopumps, fewer moving parts, and overall cheaper launch systems. It may also offer environmental advantages compared to traditional propulsion.

                      - text: 👨‍🚀 Human spaceflight is worth all the effort
                      - text: In a fascinating conversation with NASA Chief Health and Medical Officer James "JD" Polk, we discussed the risks of human spaceflight.
                      - text: While it is expensive and dangerous, the perspectives gained from human exploration — and humanity's innate drive to explore — make it worth continuing to push forward.
                      - text: ☁️ Orbital data centers are fascinating… but not imminent
                      - text: A talk by
                      - link "Gareth Stokes" [ref=e938] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/in/garethstokes/
                        - strong [ref=e940]: Gareth Stokes
                      - text: explored the idea of orbital data centers. In theory they offer advantages like unlimited solar power, natural cooling, physical security, and vast space for infrastructure.
                      - text: However, the economics aren't there yet. Even optimistic estimates suggest launching the required ~30 million kg to orbit would cost over $80 billion.

                      - text: enters an IPO this year, it could become one of the most valuable companies on the planet. More importantly, it would signal to the world that space is not a niche industry — it's the invisible backbone of modern civilisation. That kind of event could draw enormous follow-on investment into the sector.
                      - text: 🛰️ Sovereign launch capability matters more than ever
                      - text: Europe is increasingly focused on independent launch capability that doesn't rely on the US. One strong candidate for Europe's gateway to space is

                      - text: explained their hybrid propulsion system using paraffin (yes, literal candle wax) and liquid oxygen.
                      - text: Because paraffin is inert, the fuel is far safer to store and transport. Less liquid propellant also means fewer turbopumps, fewer moving parts, and overall cheaper launch systems. It may also offer environmental advantages compared to traditional propulsion.

                      - text: In a fascinating conversation with NASA Chief Health and Medical Officer James "JD" Polk, we discussed the risks of human spaceflight.
                      - text: While it is expensive and dangerous, the perspectives gained from human exploration — and humanity's innate drive to explore — make it worth continuing to push forward.
                      - text: ☁️ Orbital data centers are fascinating… but not imminent

                      - link "Gareth Stokes" [ref=e938] [cursor=pointer]:

                      - text: explored the idea of orbital data centers. In theory they offer advantages like unlimited solar power, natural cooling, physical security, and vast space for infrastructure.

                      - text: I'm convinced 2026 will redefine the global space sector.
                      - text: I spent the last two days at

                      - text: London exchanging ideas and having fascinating conversations with industry leaders.
                      - text: "Here are my biggest takeaways:"
                      - text: 🚀
                      - link "SpaceX" [ref=e914] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/spacex/
                        - strong [ref=e916]: SpaceX
                      - text: going public would be massive
                      - text: If
                      - link "SpaceX" [ref=e917] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/spacex/
                        - strong [ref=e919]: SpaceX
                      - text: enters an IPO this year, it could become one of the most valuable companies on the planet. More importantly, it would signal to the world that space is not a niche industry — it's the invisible backbone of modern civilisation. That kind of event could draw enormous follow-on investment into the sector.
                      - text: 🛰️ Sovereign launch capability matters more than ever
                      - text: Europe is increasingly focused on independent launch capability that doesn't rely on the US. One strong candidate for Europe's gateway to space is
                      - link "SaxaVord Spaceport" [ref=e920] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/saxavord/
                        - strong [ref=e922]: SaxaVord Spaceport
                      - text: ", whose remote geography makes it uniquely suited for launches — a point highlighted in a brilliant panel with"
                      - link "Debbie Strang" [ref=e923] [cursor=pointer]:

                        - strong [ref=e925]: Debbie Strang
                      - text: .
                      - text: 🔥 Hybrid propulsion could be Europe's opportunity
                      - text: During the same panel,
                      - link "Alfie Marturano" [ref=e926] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/in/alfie-marturano-b6964916/
                        - strong [ref=e928]: Alfie Marturano
                      - text: of
                      - link "HyImpulse" [ref=e929] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/hyimpulse/
                        - strong [ref=e931]: HyImpulse
                      - text: explained their hybrid propulsion system using paraffin (yes, literal candle wax) and liquid oxygen.
                      - text: Because paraffin is inert, the fuel is far safer to store and transport. Less liquid propellant also means fewer turbopumps, fewer moving parts, and overall cheaper launch systems. It may also offer environmental advantages compared to traditional propulsion.
                      - text: I had some great follow-up discussions about this with
                      - link "Ylenia M." [ref=e932] [cursor=pointer]:

                      - text: 👨‍🚀 Human spaceflight is worth all the effort
                      - text: In a fascinating conversation with NASA Chief Health and Medical Officer James "JD" Polk, we discussed the risks of human spaceflight.
                      - text: While it is expensive and dangerous, the perspectives gained from human exploration — and humanity's innate drive to explore — make it worth continuing to push forward.
                      - text: ☁️ Orbital data centers are fascinating… but not imminent
                      - text: A talk by
                      - link "Gareth Stokes" [ref=e938] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/in/garethstokes/
                        - strong [ref=e940]: Gareth Stokes
                      - text: explored the idea of orbital data centers. In theory they offer advantages like unlimited solar power, natural cooling, physical security, and vast space for infrastructure.
                      - text: However, the economics aren't there yet. Even optimistic estimates suggest launching the required ~30 million kg to orbit would cost over $80 billion.
                      - text: "The biggest thing I took away from this event:"
                      - text: The space industry is entering an incredibly exciting phase.
                      - text: Ambitious people, bold engineering challenges, and entirely new industries are forming right now — and I can't wait to be part of it.

                      - text: 🔥 Hybrid propulsion could be Europe's opportunity
                      - text: During the same panel,
                      - link "Alfie Marturano" [ref=e926] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/in/alfie-marturano-b6964916/
                        - strong [ref=e928]: Alfie Marturano
                      - text: of
                      - link "HyImpulse" [ref=e929] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/hyimpulse/
                        - strong [ref=e931]: HyImpulse
                      - text: explained their hybrid propulsion system using paraffin (yes, literal candle wax) and liquid oxygen.
                      - text: Because paraffin is inert, the fuel is far safer to store and transport. Less liquid propellant also means fewer turbopumps, fewer moving parts, and overall cheaper launch systems. It may also offer environmental advantages compared to traditional propulsion.
                      - text: I had some great follow-up discussions about this with
                      - link "Ylenia M." [ref=e932] [cursor=pointer]:

                        - strong [ref=e934]: Ylenia M.

                        - strong [ref=e937]: Titto Ephraim Mathew
                      - text: .
                      - text: 👨‍🚀 Human spaceflight is worth all the effort
                      - text: In a fascinating conversation with NASA Chief Health and Medical Officer James "JD" Polk, we discussed the risks of human spaceflight.
                      - text: While it is expensive and dangerous, the perspectives gained from human exploration — and humanity's innate drive to explore — make it worth continuing to push forward.
                      - text: ☁️ Orbital data centers are fascinating… but not imminent
                      - text: A talk by
                      - link "Gareth Stokes" [ref=e938] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/in/garethstokes/
                        - strong [ref=e940]: Gareth Stokes
                      - text: explored the idea of orbital data centers. In theory they offer advantages like unlimited solar power, natural cooling, physical security, and vast space for infrastructure.
                      - text: However, the economics aren't there yet. Even optimistic estimates suggest launching the required ~30 million kg to orbit would cost over $80 billion.
                      - text: "The biggest thing I took away from this event:"
                      - text: The space industry is entering an incredibly exciting phase.
                      - text: Ambitious people, bold engineering challenges, and entirely new industries are forming right now — and I can't wait to be part of it.

                      - text: going public would be massive

                      - text: enters an IPO this year, it could become one of the most valuable companies on the planet. More importantly, it would signal to the world that space is not a niche industry — it's the invisible backbone of modern civilisation. That kind of event could draw enormous follow-on investment into the sector.
                      - text: 🛰️ Sovereign launch capability matters more than ever
                      - text: Europe is increasingly focused on independent launch capability that doesn't rely on the US. One strong candidate for Europe's gateway to space is
                      - link "SaxaVord Spaceport" [ref=e920] [cursor=pointer]:

                      - text: During the same panel,
                      - link "Alfie Marturano" [ref=e926] [cursor=pointer]:

                        - strong [ref=e928]: Alfie Marturano

                      - text: explained their hybrid propulsion system using paraffin (yes, literal candle wax) and liquid oxygen.
                      - text: Because paraffin is inert, the fuel is far safer to store and transport. Less liquid propellant also means fewer turbopumps, fewer moving parts, and overall cheaper launch systems. It may also offer environmental advantages compared to traditional propulsion.
                      - text: I had some great follow-up discussions about this with

                      - text: 👨‍🚀 Human spaceflight is worth all the effort
                      - text: In a fascinating conversation with NASA Chief Health and Medical Officer James "JD" Polk, we discussed the risks of human spaceflight.
                      - text: While it is expensive and dangerous, the perspectives gained from human exploration — and humanity's innate drive to explore — make it worth continuing to push forward.
                      - text: ☁️ Orbital data centers are fascinating… but not imminent
                      - text: A talk by
                      - link "Gareth Stokes" [ref=e938] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/in/garethstokes/
                        - strong [ref=e940]: Gareth Stokes
                      - text: explored the idea of orbital data centers. In theory they offer advantages like unlimited solar power, natural cooling, physical security, and vast space for infrastructure.
                      - text: However, the economics aren't there yet. Even optimistic estimates suggest launching the required ~30 million kg to orbit would cost over $80 billion.
                      - text: "The biggest thing I took away from this event:"
                      - text: The space industry is entering an incredibly exciting phase.
                      - text: Ambitious people, bold engineering challenges, and entirely new industries are forming right now — and I can't wait to be part of it.

                      - text: I'm convinced 2026 will redefine the global space sector.
                      - text: I spent the last two days at
                      - link "Space-Comm" [ref=e911] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/space-comm-expo/
                        - strong [ref=e913]: Space-Comm
                      - text: London exchanging ideas and having fascinating conversations with industry leaders.
                      - text: "Here are my biggest takeaways:"
                      - text: 🚀
                      - link "SpaceX" [ref=e914] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/spacex/
                        - strong [ref=e916]: SpaceX
                      - text: going public would be massive
                      - text: If
                      - link "SpaceX" [ref=e917] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/spacex/
                        - strong [ref=e919]: SpaceX
                      - text: enters an IPO this year, it could become one of the most valuable companies on the planet. More importantly, it would signal to the world that space is not a niche industry — it's the invisible backbone of modern civilisation. That kind of event could draw enormous follow-on investment into the sector.
                      - text: 🛰️ Sovereign launch capability matters more than ever
                      - text: Europe is increasingly focused on independent launch capability that doesn't rely on the US. One strong candidate for Europe's gateway to space is
                      - link "SaxaVord Spaceport" [ref=e920] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/saxavord/
                        - strong [ref=e922]: SaxaVord Spaceport
                      - text: ", whose remote geography makes it uniquely suited for launches — a point highlighted in a brilliant panel with"
                      - link "Debbie Strang" [ref=e923] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/in/debbiestrang/
                        - strong [ref=e925]: Debbie Strang
                      - text: .
                      - text: 🔥 Hybrid propulsion could be Europe's opportunity
                      - text: During the same panel,
                      - link "Alfie Marturano" [ref=e926] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/in/alfie-marturano-b6964916/
                        - strong [ref=e928]: Alfie Marturano
                      - text: of
                      - link "HyImpulse" [ref=e929] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/hyimpulse/
                        - strong [ref=e931]: HyImpulse
                      - text: explained their hybrid propulsion system using paraffin (yes, literal candle wax) and liquid oxygen.
                      - text: Because paraffin is inert, the fuel is far safer to store and transport. Less liquid propellant also means fewer turbopumps, fewer moving parts, and overall cheaper launch systems. It may also offer environmental advantages compared to traditional propulsion.
                      - text: I had some great follow-up discussions about this with
                      - link "Ylenia M." [ref=e932] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/in/ylenia-mami/
                        - strong [ref=e934]: Ylenia M.
                      - text: and
                      - link "Titto Ephraim Mathew" [ref=e935] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/in/tittoephraimmathew/
                        - strong [ref=e937]: Titto Ephraim Mathew
                      - text: .
                      - text: 👨‍🚀 Human spaceflight is worth all the effort
                      - text: In a fascinating conversation with NASA Chief Health and Medical Officer James "JD" Polk, we discussed the risks of human spaceflight.
                      - text: While it is expensive and dangerous, the perspectives gained from human exploration — and humanity's innate drive to explore — make it worth continuing to push forward.
                      - text: ☁️ Orbital data centers are fascinating… but not imminent
                      - text: A talk by
                      - link "Gareth Stokes" [ref=e938] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/in/garethstokes/
                        - strong [ref=e940]: Gareth Stokes
                      - text: explored the idea of orbital data centers. In theory they offer advantages like unlimited solar power, natural cooling, physical security, and vast space for infrastructure.
                      - text: However, the economics aren't there yet. Even optimistic estimates suggest launching the required ~30 million kg to orbit would cost over $80 billion.
                      - text: "The biggest thing I took away from this event:"

                      - text: I'm convinced 2026 will redefine the global space sector.
                      - text: I spent the last two days at
                      - link "Space-Comm" [ref=e911] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/space-comm-expo/
                        - strong [ref=e913]: Space-Comm
                      - text: London exchanging ideas and having fascinating conversations with industry leaders.
                      - text: "Here are my biggest takeaways:"
                      - text: 🚀
                      - link "SpaceX" [ref=e914] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/spacex/
                        - strong [ref=e916]: SpaceX
                      - text: going public would be massive
                      - text: If
                      - link "SpaceX" [ref=e917] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/spacex/
                        - strong [ref=e919]: SpaceX
                      - text: enters an IPO this year, it could become one of the most valuable companies on the planet. More importantly, it would signal to the world that space is not a niche industry — it's the invisible backbone of modern civilisation. That kind of event could draw enormous follow-on investment into the sector.
                      - text: 🛰️ Sovereign launch capability matters more than ever
                      - text: Europe is increasingly focused on independent launch capability that doesn't rely on the US. One strong candidate for Europe's gateway to space is
                      - link "SaxaVord Spaceport" [ref=e920] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/saxavord/
                        - strong [ref=e922]: SaxaVord Spaceport
                      - text: ", whose remote geography makes it uniquely suited for launches — a point highlighted in a brilliant panel with"
                      - link "Debbie Strang" [ref=e923] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/in/debbiestrang/
                        - strong [ref=e925]: Debbie Strang
                      - text: .
                      - text: 🔥 Hybrid propulsion could be Europe's opportunity
                      - text: During the same panel,
                      - link "Alfie Marturano" [ref=e926] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/in/alfie-marturano-b6964916/
                        - strong [ref=e928]: Alfie Marturano
                      - text: of
                      - link "HyImpulse" [ref=e929] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/hyimpulse/
                        - strong [ref=e931]: HyImpulse
                      - text: explained their hybrid propulsion system using paraffin (yes, literal candle wax) and liquid oxygen.
                      - text: Because paraffin is inert, the fuel is far safer to store and transport. Less liquid propellant also means fewer turbopumps, fewer moving parts, and overall cheaper launch systems. It may also offer environmental advantages compared to traditional propulsion.
                      - text: I had some great follow-up discussions about this with
                      - link "Ylenia M." [ref=e932] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/in/ylenia-mami/
                        - strong [ref=e934]: Ylenia M.
                      - text: and
                      - link "Titto Ephraim Mathew" [ref=e935] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/in/tittoephraimmathew/
                        - strong [ref=e937]: Titto Ephraim Mathew
                      - text: .
                      - text: 👨‍🚀 Human spaceflight is worth all the effort
                      - text: In a fascinating conversation with NASA Chief Health and Medical Officer James "JD" Polk, we discussed the risks of human spaceflight.
                      - text: While it is expensive and dangerous, the perspectives gained from human exploration — and humanity's innate drive to explore — make it worth continuing to push forward.
                      - text: ☁️ Orbital data centers are fascinating… but not imminent
                      - text: A talk by
                      - link "Gareth Stokes" [ref=e938] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/in/garethstokes/
                        - strong [ref=e940]: Gareth Stokes
                      - text: explored the idea of orbital data centers. In theory they offer advantages like unlimited solar power, natural cooling, physical security, and vast space for infrastructure.
                      - text: However, the economics aren't there yet. Even optimistic estimates suggest launching the required ~30 million kg to orbit would cost over $80 billion.
                      - text: "The biggest thing I took away from this event:"

                      - text: I'm convinced 2026 will redefine the global space sector.

                      - text: enters an IPO this year, it could become one of the most valuable companies on the planet. More importantly, it would signal to the world that space is not a niche industry — it's the invisible backbone of modern civilisation. That kind of event could draw enormous follow-on investment into the sector.
                      - text: 🛰️ Sovereign launch capability matters more than ever
                      - text: Europe is increasingly focused on independent launch capability that doesn't rely on the US. One strong candidate for Europe's gateway to space is
                      - link "SaxaVord Spaceport" [ref=e920] [cursor=pointer]:

                      - text: During the same panel,
                      - link "Alfie Marturano" [ref=e926] [cursor=pointer]:

                        - strong [ref=e928]: Alfie Marturano

                      - text: explained their hybrid propulsion system using paraffin (yes, literal candle wax) and liquid oxygen.
                      - text: Because paraffin is inert, the fuel is far safer to store and transport. Less liquid propellant also means fewer turbopumps, fewer moving parts, and overall cheaper launch systems. It may also offer environmental advantages compared to traditional propulsion.
                      - text: I had some great follow-up discussions about this with

                      - text: 👨‍🚀 Human spaceflight is worth all the effort
                      - text: In a fascinating conversation with NASA Chief Health and Medical Officer James "JD" Polk, we discussed the risks of human spaceflight.
                      - text: While it is expensive and dangerous, the perspectives gained from human exploration — and humanity's innate drive to explore — make it worth continuing to push forward.
                      - text: ☁️ Orbital data centers are fascinating… but not imminent
                      - text: A talk by
                      - link "Gareth Stokes" [ref=e938] [cursor=pointer]:
                        - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/in/garethstokes/
                        - strong [ref=e940]: Gareth Stokes
                      - text: explored the idea of orbital data centers. In theory they offer advantages like unlimited solar power, natural cooling, physical security, and vast space for infrastructure.
                      - text: However, the economics aren't there yet. Even optimistic estimates suggest launching the required ~30 million kg to orbit would cost over $80 billion.
                      - text: "The biggest thing I took away from this event:"
                      - text: The space industry is entering an incredibly exciting phase.
                      - text: Ambitious people, bold engineering challenges, and entirely new industries are forming right now — and I can't wait to be part of it.

            - text: I'm convinced 2026 will redefine the global space sector. I spent the last two days at
            - link "Space-Comm" [ref=e164]:
            - text: "London exchanging ideas and having fascinating conversations with industry leaders. Here are my biggest takeaways: 🚀"
            - link "SpaceX" [ref=e165]:
            - text: going public would be massive If
            - link "SpaceX" [ref=e166] [nth=1]:
            - text: enters an IPO this year, it could become one of the most valuable companies on the planet. More importantly, it would signal to the world that space is not a niche industry — it's the invisible backbone of modern civilisation. That kind of event could draw enormous follow-on investment into the sector. 🛰️ Sovereign launch capability matters more than ever Europe is increasingly focused on independent launch capability that doesn't rely on the US. One strong candidate for Europe's gateway to space is
            - link "SaxaVord Spaceport" [ref=e167]:
            - text: ", whose remote geography makes it uniquely suited for launches — a point highlighted in a brilliant panel with"
            - link "Debbie Strang" [ref=e168]:
            - text: . 🔥 Hybrid propulsion could be Europe's opportunity During the same panel,
            - link "Alfie Marturano" [ref=e169]:
            - text: of
            - link "HyImpulse" [ref=e170]:
            - text: explained their hybrid propulsion system using paraffin (yes, literal candle wax) and liquid oxygen. Because paraffin is inert, the fuel is far safer to store and transport. Less liquid propellant also means fewer turbopumps, fewer moving parts, and overall cheaper launch systems. It may also offer environmental advantages compared to traditional propulsion. I had some great follow-up discussions about this with
            - link "Ylenia M." [ref=e171]:
            - text: and
            - link "Titto Ephraim Mathew" [ref=e172]:
            - text: . 👨‍🚀 Human spaceflight is worth all the effort In a fascinating conversation with NASA Chief Health and Medical Officer James "JD" Polk, we discussed the risks of human spaceflight. While it is expensive and dangerous, the perspectives gained from human exploration — and humanity's innate drive to explore — make it worth continuing to push forward. ☁️ Orbital data centers are fascinating… but not imminent A talk by
            - link "Gareth Stokes" [ref=e173]:
            - text: "explored the idea of orbital data centers. In theory they offer advantages like unlimited solar power, natural cooling, physical security, and vast space for infrastructure. However, the economics aren't there yet. Even optimistic estimates suggest launching the required ~30 million kg to orbit would cost over $80 billion. The biggest thing I took away from this event: The space industry is entering an incredibly exciting phase. Ambitious people, bold engineering challenges, and entirely new industries are forming right now — and I can't wait to be part of it."

            - text: I'm convinced 2026 will redefine the global space sector. I spent the last two days at
            - link "Space-Comm" [ref=e164]:
            - text: "London exchanging ideas and having fascinating conversations with industry leaders. Here are my biggest takeaways: 🚀"
            - link "SpaceX" [ref=e165]:
            - text: going public would be massive If
            - link "SpaceX" [ref=e166] [nth=1]:
            - text: enters an IPO this year, it could become one of the most valuable companies on the planet. More importantly, it would signal to the world that space is not a niche industry — it's the invisible backbone of modern civilisation. That kind of event could draw enormous follow-on investment into the sector. 🛰️ Sovereign launch capability matters more than ever Europe is increasingly focused on independent launch capability that doesn't rely on the US. One strong candidate for Europe's gateway to space is
            - link "SaxaVord Spaceport" [ref=e167]:
            - text: ", whose remote geography makes it uniquely suited for launches — a point highlighted in a brilliant panel with"
            - link "Debbie Strang" [ref=e168]:
            - text: . 🔥 Hybrid propulsion could be Europe's opportunity During the same panel,
            - link "Alfie Marturano" [ref=e169]:
            - text: of
            - link "HyImpulse" [ref=e170]:
            - text: explained their hybrid propulsion system using paraffin (yes, literal candle wax) and liquid oxygen. Because paraffin is inert, the fuel is far safer to store and transport. Less liquid propellant also means fewer turbopumps, fewer moving parts, and overall cheaper launch systems. It may also offer environmental advantages compared to traditional propulsion. I had some great follow-up discussions about this with
            - link "Ylenia M." [ref=e171]:
            - text: and
            - link "Titto Ephraim Mathew" [ref=e172]:
            - text: . 👨‍🚀 Human spaceflight is worth all the effort In a fascinating conversation with NASA Chief Health and Medical Officer James "JD" Polk, we discussed the risks of human spaceflight. While it is expensive and dangerous, the perspectives gained from human exploration — and humanity's innate drive to explore — make it worth continuing to push forward. ☁️ Orbital data centers are fascinating… but not imminent A talk by
            - link "Gareth Stokes" [ref=e173]:
            - text: "explored the idea of orbital data centers. In theory they offer advantages like unlimited solar power, natural cooling, physical security, and vast space for infrastructure. However, the economics aren't there yet. Even optimistic estimates suggest launching the required ~30 million kg to orbit would cost over $80 billion. The biggest thing I took away from this event: The space industry is entering an incredibly exciting phase. Ambitious people, bold engineering challenges, and entirely new industries are forming right now — and I can't wait to be part of it."

            - text: I'm convinced 2026 will redefine the global space sector. I spent the last two days at
            - link "Space-Comm" [ref=e165]:
            - text: "London exchanging ideas and having fascinating conversations with industry leaders. Here are my biggest takeaways: 🚀"
            - link "SpaceX" [ref=e166]:
            - text: going public would be massive If
            - link "SpaceX" [ref=e167] [nth=1]:
            - text: enters an IPO this year, it could become one of the most valuable companies on the planet. More importantly, it would signal to the world that space is not a niche industry — it's the invisible backbone of modern civilisation. That kind of event could draw enormous follow-on investment into the sector. 🛰️ Sovereign launch capability matters more than ever Europe is increasingly focused on independent launch capability that doesn't rely on the US. One strong candidate for Europe's gateway to space is
            - link "SaxaVord Spaceport" [ref=e168]:
            - text: ", whose remote geography makes it uniquely suited for launches — a point highlighted in a brilliant panel with"
            - link "Debbie Strang" [ref=e169]:
            - text: . 🔥 Hybrid propulsion could be Europe's opportunity During the same panel,
            - link "Alfie Marturano" [ref=e170]:
            - text: of
            - link "HyImpulse" [ref=e171]:
            - text: explained their hybrid propulsion system using paraffin (yes, literal candle wax) and liquid oxygen. Because paraffin is inert, the fuel is far safer to store and transport. Less liquid propellant also means fewer turbopumps, fewer moving parts, and overall cheaper launch systems. It may also offer environmental advantages compared to traditional propulsion. I had some great follow-up discussions about this with
            - link "Ylenia M." [ref=e172]:
            - text: and
            - link "Titto Ephraim Mathew" [ref=e173]:
            - text: . 👨‍🚀 Human spaceflight is worth all the effort In a fascinating conversation with NASA Chief Health and Medical Officer James "JD" Polk, we discussed the risks of human spaceflight. While it is expensive and dangerous, the perspectives gained from human exploration — and humanity's innate drive to explore — make it worth continuing to push forward. ☁️ Orbital data centers are fascinating… but not imminent A talk by
            - link "Gareth Stokes" [ref=e174]:
            - text: "explored the idea of orbital data centers. In theory they offer advantages like unlimited solar power, natural cooling, physical security, and vast space for infrastructure. However, the economics aren't there yet. Even optimistic estimates suggest launching the required ~30 million kg to orbit would cost over $80 billion. The biggest thing I took away from this event: The space industry is entering an incredibly exciting phase. Ambitious people, bold engineering challenges, and entirely new industries are forming right now — and I can't wait to be part of it."

            - text: I'm convinced 2026 will redefine the global space sector. I spent the last two days at
            - link "Space-Comm" [ref=e165]:
            - text: "London exchanging ideas and having fascinating conversations with industry leaders. Here are my biggest takeaways: 🚀"
            - link "SpaceX" [ref=e166]:
            - text: going public would be massive If
            - link "SpaceX" [ref=e167] [nth=1]:
            - text: enters an IPO this year, it could become one of the most valuable companies on the planet. More importantly, it would signal to the world that space is not a niche industry — it's the invisible backbone of modern civilisation. That kind of event could draw enormous follow-on investment into the sector. 🛰️ Sovereign launch capability matters more than ever Europe is increasingly focused on independent launch capability that doesn't rely on the US. One strong candidate for Europe's gateway to space is
            - link "SaxaVord Spaceport" [ref=e168]:
            - text: ", whose remote geography makes it uniquely suited for launches — a point highlighted in a brilliant panel with"
            - link "Debbie Strang" [ref=e169]:
            - text: . 🔥 Hybrid propulsion could be Europe's opportunity During the same panel,
            - link "Alfie Marturano" [ref=e170]:
            - text: of
            - link "HyImpulse" [ref=e171]:
            - text: explained their hybrid propulsion system using paraffin (yes, literal candle wax) and liquid oxygen. Because paraffin is inert, the fuel is far safer to store and transport. Less liquid propellant also means fewer turbopumps, fewer moving parts, and overall cheaper launch systems. It may also offer environmental advantages compared to traditional propulsion. I had some great follow-up discussions about this with
            - link "Ylenia M." [ref=e172]:
            - text: and
            - link "Titto Ephraim Mathew" [ref=e173]:
            - text: . 👨‍🚀 Human spaceflight is worth all the effort In a fascinating conversation with NASA Chief Health and Medical Officer James "JD" Polk, we discussed the risks of human spaceflight. While it is expensive and dangerous, the perspectives gained from human exploration — and humanity's innate drive to explore — make it worth continuing to push forward. ☁️ Orbital data centers are fascinating… but not imminent A talk by
            - link "Gareth Stokes" [ref=e174]:
            - text: "explored the idea of orbital data centers. In theory they offer advantages like unlimited solar power, natural cooling, physical security, and vast space for infrastructure. However, the economics aren't there yet. Even optimistic estimates suggest launching the required ~30 million kg to orbit would cost over $80 billion. The biggest thing I took away from this event: The space industry is entering an incredibly exciting phase. Ambitious people, bold engineering challenges, and entirely new industries are forming right now — and I can't wait to be part of it."

            - text: I'm convinced 2026 will redefine the global space sector. I spent the last two days at
            - link "Space-Comm" [ref=e170]:
            - text: "London exchanging ideas and having fascinating conversations with industry leaders. Here are my biggest takeaways: 🚀"
            - link "SpaceX" [ref=e171]:
            - text: going public would be massive If
            - link "SpaceX" [ref=e172] [nth=1]:
            - text: enters an IPO this year, it could become one of the most valuable companies on the planet. More importantly, it would signal to the world that space is not a niche industry — it's the invisible backbone of modern civilisation. That kind of event could draw enormous follow-on investment into the sector. 🛰️ Sovereign launch capability matters more than ever Europe is increasingly focused on independent launch capability that doesn't rely on the US. One strong candidate for Europe's gateway to space is
            - link "SaxaVord Spaceport" [ref=e173]:
            - text: ", whose remote geography makes it uniquely suited for launches — a point highlighted in a brilliant panel with"
            - link "Debbie Strang" [ref=e174]:
            - text: . 🔥 Hybrid propulsion could be Europe's opportunity During the same panel,
            - link "Alfie Marturano" [ref=e175]:
            - text: of
            - link "HyImpulse" [ref=e176]:
            - text: explained their hybrid propulsion system using paraffin (yes, literal candle wax) and liquid oxygen. Because paraffin is inert, the fuel is far safer to store and transport. Less liquid propellant also means fewer turbopumps, fewer moving parts, and overall cheaper launch systems. It may also offer environmental advantages compared to traditional propulsion. I had some great follow-up discussions about this with
            - link "Ylenia M." [ref=e177]:
            - text: and
            - link "Titto Ephraim Mathew" [ref=e178]:
            - text: . 👨‍🚀 Human spaceflight is worth all the effort In a fascinating conversation with NASA Chief Health and Medical Officer James "JD" Polk, we discussed the risks of human spaceflight. While it is expensive and dangerous, the perspectives gained from human exploration — and humanity's innate drive to explore — make it worth continuing to push forward. ☁️ Orbital data centers are fascinating… but not imminent A talk by
            - link "Gareth Stokes" [ref=e179]:
            - text: "explored the idea of orbital data centers. In theory they offer advantages like unlimited solar power, natural cooling, physical security, and vast space for infrastructure. However, the economics aren't there yet. Even optimistic estimates suggest launching the required ~30 million kg to orbit would cost over $80 billion. The biggest thing I took away from this event: The space industry is entering an incredibly exciting phase. Ambitious people, bold engineering challenges, and entirely new industries are forming right now — and I can't wait to be part of it."

            - text: I'm convinced 2026 will redefine the global space sector. I spent the last two days at

            - text: "London exchanging ideas and having fascinating conversations with industry leaders. Here are my biggest takeaways: 🚀"
            - link "SpaceX" [ref=e171]:
            - text: going public would be massive If
            - link "SpaceX" [ref=e172] [nth=1]:
            - text: enters an IPO this year, it could become one of the most valuable companies on the planet. More importantly, it would signal to the world that space is not a niche industry — it's the invisible backbone of modern civilisation. That kind of event could draw enormous follow-on investment into the sector. 🛰️ Sovereign launch capability matters more than ever Europe is increasingly focused on independent launch capability that doesn't rely on the US. One strong candidate for Europe's gateway to space is
            - link "SaxaVord Spaceport" [ref=e173]:
            - text: ", whose remote geography makes it uniquely suited for launches — a point highlighted in a brilliant panel with"
            - link "Debbie Strang" [ref=e174]:
            - text: . 🔥 Hybrid propulsion could be Europe's opportunity During the same panel,
            - link "Alfie Marturano" [ref=e175]:
            - text: of
            - link "HyImpulse" [ref=e176]:
            - text: explained their hybrid propulsion system using paraffin (yes, literal candle wax) and liquid oxygen. Because paraffin is inert, the fuel is far safer to store and transport. Less liquid propellant also means fewer turbopumps, fewer moving parts, and overall cheaper launch systems. It may also offer environmental advantages compared to traditional propulsion. I had some great follow-up discussions about this with
            - link "Ylenia M." [ref=e177]:
            - text: and
            - link "Titto Ephraim Mathew" [ref=e178]:
            - text: . 👨‍🚀 Human spaceflight is worth all the effort In a fascinating conversation with NASA Chief Health and Medical Officer James "JD" Polk, we discussed the risks of human spaceflight. While it is expensive and dangerous, the perspectives gained from human exploration — and humanity's innate drive to explore — make it worth continuing to push forward. ☁️ Orbital data centers are fascinating… but not imminent A talk by
            - link "Gareth Stokes" [ref=e179]:
            - text: "explored the idea of orbital data centers. In theory they offer advantages like unlimited solar power, natural cooling, physical security, and vast space for infrastructure. However, the economics aren't there yet. Even optimistic estimates suggest launching the required ~30 million kg to orbit would cost over $80 billion. The biggest thing I took away from this event: The space industry is entering an incredibly exciting phase. Ambitious people, bold engineering challenges, and entirely new industries are forming right now — and I can't wait to be part of it."

            - text: I'm convinced 2026 will redefine the global space sector. I spent the last two days at

          - paragraph:
            - text: I'm convinced 2026 will redefine the global space sector. I spent the last two days at
            - link "Space-Comm" [ref=e170]:
              - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/space-comm-expo/
              - strong: Space-Comm
            - text: "London exchanging ideas and having fascinating conversations with industry leaders. Here are my biggest takeaways: 🚀"
            - link "SpaceX" [ref=e171]:
              - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/spacex/
              - strong: SpaceX
            - text: going public would be massive If
            - link "SpaceX" [ref=e172] [nth=1]:
              - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/spacex/
              - strong: SpaceX
            - text: enters an IPO this year, it could become one of the most valuable companies on the planet. More importantly, it would signal to the world that space is not a niche industry — it's the invisible backbone of modern civilisation. That kind of event could draw enormous follow-on investment into the sector. 🛰️ Sovereign launch capability matters more than ever Europe is increasingly focused on independent launch capability that doesn't rely on the US. One strong candidate for Europe's gateway to space is
            - link "SaxaVord Spaceport" [ref=e173]:
              - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/saxavord/
              - strong: SaxaVord Spaceport
            - text: ", whose remote geography makes it uniquely suited for launches — a point highlighted in a brilliant panel with"
            - link "Debbie Strang" [ref=e174]:
              - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/in/debbiestrang/
              - strong: Debbie Strang
            - text: . 🔥 Hybrid propulsion could be Europe's opportunity During the same panel,
            - link "Alfie Marturano" [ref=e175]:
              - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/in/alfie-marturano-b6964916/
              - strong: Alfie Marturano
            - text: of
            - link "HyImpulse" [ref=e176]:
              - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/company/hyimpulse/
              - strong: HyImpulse
            - text: explained their hybrid propulsion system using paraffin (yes, literal candle wax) and liquid oxygen. Because paraffin is inert, the fuel is far safer to store and transport. Less liquid propellant also means fewer turbopumps, fewer moving parts, and overall cheaper launch systems. It may also offer environmental advantages compared to traditional propulsion. I had some great follow-up discussions about this with
            - link "Ylenia M." [ref=e177]:
              - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/in/ylenia-mami/
              - strong: Ylenia M.
            - text: and
            - link "Titto Ephraim Mathew" [ref=e178]:
              - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/in/tittoephraimmathew/
              - strong: Titto Ephraim Mathew
            - text: . 👨‍🚀 Human spaceflight is worth all the effort In a fascinating conversation with NASA Chief Health and Medical Officer James "JD" Polk, we discussed the risks of human spaceflight. While it is expensive and dangerous, the perspectives gained from human exploration — and humanity's innate drive to explore — make it worth continuing to push forward. ☁️ Orbital data centers are fascinating… but not imminent A talk by
            - link "Gareth Stokes" [ref=e179]:
              - /url: https://www.linkedin.com/in/garethstokes/
              - strong: Gareth Stokes
            - text: "explored the idea of orbital data centers. In theory they offer advantages like unlimited solar power, natural cooling, physical security, and vast space for infrastructure. However, the economics aren't there yet. Even optimistic estimates suggest launching the required ~30 million kg to orbit would cost over $80 billion. The biggest thing I took away from this event: The space industry is entering an incredibly exciting phase. Ambitious people, bold engineering challenges, and entirely new industries are forming right now — and I can't wait to be part of it."

            - text: I'm convinced 2026 will redefine the global space sector. I spent the last two days at
            - link "Space-Comm" [ref=e170]:
            - text: "London exchanging ideas and having fascinating conversations with industry leaders. Here are my biggest takeaways: 🚀"
            - link "SpaceX" [ref=e171]:
            - text: going public would be massive If
            - link "SpaceX" [ref=e172] [nth=1]:
            - text: enters an IPO this year, it could become one of the most valuable companies on the planet. More importantly, it would signal to the world that space is not a niche industry — it's the invisible backbone of modern civilisation. That kind of event could draw enormous follow-on investment into the sector. 🛰️ Sovereign launch capability matters more than ever Europe is increasingly focused on independent launch capability that doesn't rely on the US. One strong candidate for Europe's gateway to space is
            - link "SaxaVord Spaceport" [ref=e173]:
            - text: ", whose remote geography makes it uniquely suited for launches — a point highlighted in a brilliant panel with"
            - link "Debbie Strang" [ref=e174]:
            - text: . 🔥 Hybrid propulsion could be Europe's opportunity During the same panel,
            - link "Alfie Marturano" [ref=e175]:
            - text: of
            - link "HyImpulse" [ref=e176]:
            - text: explained their hybrid propulsion system using paraffin (yes, literal candle wax) and liquid oxygen. Because paraffin is inert, the fuel is far safer to store and transport. Less liquid propellant also means fewer turbopumps, fewer moving parts, and overall cheaper launch systems. It may also offer environmental advantages compared to traditional propulsion. I had some great follow-up discussions about this with
            - link "Ylenia M." [ref=e177]:
            - text: and
            - link "Titto Ephraim Mathew" [ref=e178]:
            - text: . 👨‍🚀 Human spaceflight is worth all the effort In a fascinating conversation with NASA Chief Health and Medical Officer James "JD" Polk, we discussed the risks of human spaceflight. While it is expensive and dangerous, the perspectives gained from human exploration — and humanity's innate drive to explore — make it worth continuing to push forward. ☁️ Orbital data centers are fascinating… but not imminent A talk by
            - link "Gareth Stokes" [ref=e179]:
            - text: "explored the idea of orbital data centers. In theory they offer advantages like unlimited solar power, natural cooling, physical security, and vast space for infrastructure. However, the economics aren't there yet. Even optimistic estimates suggest launching the required ~30 million kg to orbit would cost over $80 billion. The biggest thing I took away from this event: The space industry is entering an incredibly exciting phase. Ambitious people, bold engineering challenges, and entirely new industries are forming right now — and I can't wait to be part of it."

            - text: I'm convinced 2026 will redefine the global space sector. I spent the last two days at
